message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on Pacific Avenue in this auction.

I have $670 and own three properties. Pacific Avenue costs $300. No greens are owned yet, so buying it won't complete a monopoly immediately.

p2 started the auction with only $11 cash after heavy dark-blue building. p4 has $1395 and owns light blues plus railroads. p1 has $854 and owns orange properties plus utilities. The yellows are split between p3 and p4.

Completing the green set would require North Carolina and Pennsylvania, plus heavy building costs. That is too much capital for my $670. p2 cannot bid much with only $11. p4 may want greens as a long-term asset or to block others. I should avoid overpaying.

Completing the pink set is the most practical path. I already own St. Charles Place, so I only need States and Virginia. The brown set is also cheap to finish with Baltic and Mediterranean. Buying Pacific would waste too much cash on a single green property. p2 cannot bid above about $11.

I could bid a modest amount to try for a cheap Pacific Avenue, but p1 and p4 have more cash and may want the green set. A fight with them would drain my $670. I might be better off dropping out.

Boardwalk with two houses pays $600. Park Place with one house pays $175. p2 is a rent threat, but with only $11 cash they could bankrupt themselves if they land on expensive properties.

I will bid $1 on Pacific Avenue. This is a free option to win cheaply if others drop out, or to reassess later if someone bids higher. I need to preserve my $670 for survival and future acquisitions.

I will keep my public message neutral to avoid signaling strong interest. I am also weighing whether to bid more aggressively against p4, who has $1395 and almost owns the light-blue set.

A $300 bid on Pacific Avenue would bankrupt me if I land on Boardwalk with two houses, since that rent is $600 and I would have only $70 left. I cannot outbid p4's $1395 with my $670, so I must avoid spending more than about $70 on this auction.

Mortgaging all three owned properties yields $230 in extra cash. That allows spending up to about $450 on Pacific Avenue while still surviving a Boardwalk rent of $600. The remaining cash would be only $70, leaving me severely undercapitalized.
